title: Diverse Intra- and Inter-Domain Activity Style Fusion for Cross-Person Generalization in Activity Recognition

problem.claim: Cross-person activity-recognition generalization methods struggle to capture intra- and inter-domain style diversity, leaving gaps with the target domain.

gap.claim: Existing domain-generalization methods do not sufficiently address domain gaps caused by limited intra- and inter-domain style diversity.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes domain padding, which synthesizes intra- and inter-domain style data to enrich domain diversity while maintaining robustness to class labels.
The approach instantiates domain padding with a conditional diffusion model and a style-fused sampling strategy that can use one or more random styles to guide synthesis.
Style-fused sampling uses permutations and combinations of existing styles to generate diverse new style instances.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish domain padding as a novel perspective and style-fused sampling as an advancement over traditional condition-guided sampling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across a broad range of datasets, the generated data is reported to achieve substantial diversity within the domain space.
Both intra-domain and inter-domain generated data are reported to contribute to performance improvements of varying degrees.
The approach is reported to outperform state-of-the-art domain-generalization methods on all evaluated human-activity-recognition tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing methods have difficulty modeling intra- and inter-domain style diversity for cross-person generalization.
The paper frames synthetic enrichment of domain diversity as domain padding.
A conditional diffusion model with style-fused sampling generates data guided by one or more random styles and combinations of existing styles.
The authors report diverse generated data, performance gains from both style types, and superiority to state-of-the-art domain-generalization methods.

source_observation.claim: Combining intra-domain and inter-domain styles is reported to improve the diversity of synthesized data and downstream performance.

interpretation.claim: Synthetic variation may be more useful when it represents both within-domain and across-domain style differences.

application.claim: For cross-person activity-recognition systems, generate training examples using multiple style sources while preserving class-label conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which datasets, style combinations, or task conditions are necessary for the reported gains.

unknowns: Specific datasets, task splits, evaluation metrics, and baseline configurations are not provided.
The conditional diffusion architecture, training procedure, and label-robustness mechanism are not described.
The magnitude and statistical reliability of the reported performance improvements are not provided.
